rover_tire_pressure._note: M3a, researched 2026-11-22 then [PLACEHOLDER] until playtest: MPE ±0.5 % of a 100 psi span (3.45 kPa) and 0.1 psi steps (0.69 kPa), from the JACO Elite 100 PSI digital tire gauge. Drift is a game pace (MPE in about 25 days; usage drift scaled with the MPE), much faster than the stability a Honeywell ABP 100PG class sensor is specified for. AUD-1T's tire checks are the canon hook.

dome_pressure._note: M3a, researched 2026-11-22 then [PLACEHOLDER] until playtest: WIKA CPG1200 digital absolute gauge, 0 kPa to 160 kPa, ±0.25 % of span (0.40 kPa), 0.01 kPa display. Drift is a game pace (MPE in about 17 days), much faster than the gauge's specified long-term stability. Against the WD-1 the TUR is 3.11:1, under 4:1 on purpose (Ryan, 2026-11-22); the HB-700 (Tier 3) is its proper reference.

terrarium_thermometer._note: M3a, researched 2026-11-22 then [PLACEHOLDER] until playtest: a Pt100 RTD probe (Vaisala TMP115, ±0.25 °C over this range) on a TMT130-class transmitter; ±0.5 °C is the chosen game MPE, leaving room for the analog output and readout. 0.1 °C display (Testo 108 class). The FM-3 checks its 0 V to 10 V output, scaled to 0 °C to 50 °C, so 5 °C/V (standard_sensitivity converts the standard's volts into this unit's degrees Celsius). Drift is a game pace (MPE in about 25 days).

relay_timebase._note: M3a, researched 2026-11-22 then [PLACEHOLDER] until playtest: fractional frequency scaled by 10⁻⁶. The game MPE of ±1.0 × 10⁻⁶ and readout step of 0.01 × 10⁻⁶ are proposed limits for a Stratum 3 OCXO (CTS Model 137 class, ±0.5 × 10⁻⁶ annual aging) read on a reciprocal counter (Keysight 53230A class). Drift is a game pace. Its standard, the Rb-2D, is not sold yet; until the colony has one it is out of service: it does not drift and is not audited.

rotary_table._note: Tier 0 angle standard (Ryan, 2026-11-22). Name picked by Ryan 2026-11-22 (no trademark search yet); every number here is a game placeholder, not from a datasheet. spec_confidence_pct null = no stated confidence, so the spec is rectangular (half-width / √3).

humidity_generator._note: Tier 0 humidity standard, two-pressure generator class (Ryan, 2026-11-22). Name picked by Ryan 2026-11-22 (no trademark search yet); every number here is a game placeholder, not from a datasheet.

field_meter_dc._note: Tier 1, sold by Bram after the first clean audit (spec section 1.4 #1). Researched 2026-11-22: Fluke 87V MAX class 4½-digit handheld, 60 V range in HiRes mode. At 10 V, 0.05 % of reading is 5 mV and 10 counts are 10 mV, so the MPE is 15 mV; 1 mV resolution. The 0.7 mV certificate uncertainty (k = 2) is an estimated lab budget: a Fluke 5560A-class calibrator adds about 0.072 mV, the rest is resolution and repeatability. Drift takes it to its MPE in about 120 days (Ryan, 2026-11-22); Fluke specifies its accuracy for two years under stated conditions. Price and interval are game balance [PLACEHOLDER]. It is both the player's handheld and, until the colony has an HM-3, a standard calibrated only at OIRM; with one it can also be calibrated on the bench (60 min [PLACEHOLDER]).

reference_gauge._note: Tier 1, sold by Bram after the first clean audit (spec section 1.4 #7). Researched 2026-11-22: WIKA CPG1500 class precision digital test gauge, 0 kPa to 250 kPa, ±0.05 % of span (0.125 kPa) with the measuring rate at up to three readings per second; 0.01 kPa display. WIKA states the accuracy at k = 2, which the game enters as spec_confidence_pct 95. The 0.03 kPa certificate uncertainty (k = 2) is an estimated lab budget: a Mensor CPC8000-class controller adds about 0.020 kPa, the rest is readout and repeatability. Drift takes it to its MPE in about 120 days (Ryan, 2026-11-22); WIKA recommends a one-year calibration interval, depending on use. Price and interval are game balance [PLACEHOLDER]. With an HB-700 on the colony it can also be calibrated on the bench (60 min [PLACEHOLDER]).

multi_source_calibrator._note: Tier 2 (spec section 1.4 #3): calibrates the FM-3 on the bench. Sold by Kestrel on solar flare nights, with no certificate. The MPE is the cited best-case DC voltage class spec, 6 µV/V (1 year, 95 %), at the 10 V test point; the floor and other ranges are not modeled. Certificate uncertainty, drift (MPE in about 120 days), resolution, price and interval are [PLACEHOLDER].

torque_standard._note: Tier 2 (spec section 1.4), sold by Bram once there is an OIRM account. ±0.25 % of indicated from 10 % to 100 % of full scale (retailer-cited, Ryan's pick), taken at a 100 N·m test point [PLACEHOLDER]. It calibrates the robots' grip torque sensors; Bram's wrench is not in the game yet. Certificate uncertainty, drift (MPE in about 120 days), resolution, price and interval are [PLACEHOLDER].

pressure_controller.display_name: Hellas Basin Controls HB-700 Pressure Controller
pressure_controller._note: Tier 3 bench pressure controller (spec section 1.4 #6), offered early and at a discount by the first OIRM credibility contract (Ryan, 2026-11-22). Cited class spec: 0.008 % of reading (Mensor CPC8000 IntelliScale), about 0.008 kPa at a 100 kPa dome reading; the 0.01 kPa MPE rounds that up and is [PLACEHOLDER], as are the certificate uncertainty, drift (MPE in about 120 days), price and interval. takes_over: units whose standard becomes this one when it is bought (the dome gauge, which only reaches 3.11:1 against the WD-1). The tire gauge stays on the WD-1 for field calibration. It also calibrates the WD-1 on the bench. Outside the contract it is Kestrel's to sell [ASSUMPTION].

rubidium_reference._note: Tier 3 (spec section 1.4 #4): calibrates the relay timebase. relay_disciplined: while some rover has line of sight to the relay it is locked to OIRM time and does not drift; otherwise it is in holdover, drifts at its aging rate, and its certificate lapses after initial_interval_days (3 [PLACEHOLDER]) until it locks again. It never goes to OIRM. Cited class spec: aging under 2 × 10⁻¹² per day (typical), and under 3 × 10⁻¹⁰ over 0 °C to 50 °C, used here as the MPE. Certificate uncertainty, resolution, display and price are [PLACEHOLDER]. Old Orin supplies it [ASSUMPTION]; Orin is not in the game, so it can't be bought yet.

soil_probe._note: Income milestone (Ryan, 2026-11-22: 'New soil probe'). Auto-irrigation holds each plot at its set point as this probe reads it, so the soil's true volumetric water content is the set point minus the probe's error. The 3.0 % MPE (0.03 m³/m³) follows the generic-calibration accuracy commonly stated for capacitance soil-moisture probes; drift (MPE in 20 days), residual, resolution and bench time are game pace. All [PLACEHOLDER] until Ryan sets them.

gravimetric_kit._note: Tier 0 reference for the soil probe: soil samples weighed wet, oven-dried and weighed again (the gravimetric method), with a certified balance. Agent's proposal, not yet Ryan's; no maker name. Every number is [PLACEHOLDER]; drift takes it to its MPE in about 60 days like the other Tier 0 standards.

instruments._note: role unit = audited and calibrated at the bench against calibrated_by; role standard = Tier 0 reference, drifts, audited for a lapsed certificate only (not while at OIRM); starts with a founding-stock OIRM certificate. Tier 0 standards' daily_drift_rate takes one from zero to its MPE in about 60 days, Tier 1 in about 120 days (Ryan, 2026-11-22), so skipping an OIRM cycle risks a recall. resolution (one digit of the unit under test), bench_minutes and the standards' specs and drift rates are placeholders (docs/design/equipment_skills_robots.md section 1.5). tier 0 (or absent) = owned from the start; tier 1+ = bought, arrives with a maker's certificate traceable to OIRM (section 1.7). A unit is in service (audited, on the bench) only while its calibrated_by standard is owned. standard_sensitivity (default 1) converts the standard's unit into the unit's own. display_decimals sets how many decimals readings show.

robot_sensors._note: One copy per built robot, with the id sensor@robot (robots.json). Audited only once the robot is released. Every number is [PLACEHOLDER], chosen so each TUR is at least 4:1 against calibrated_by (all sensors drift to their MPE in about 30 days). The soil probe reads a voltage: 5 percentage points of VWC per volt from the FM-3 [ASSUMPTION].

compliance_fine._note: suspect_cal_credits: a unit whose calibration was made suspect by a recall and not redone before the audit (milestone 2). Placeholder. aud1t_tire_*: AUD-1T measures the rover tires on audit day (Ryan, 2026-11-22: 'AUD-1T's own line'); tires are filled to what the tire gauge reads, so they sit off the set point by minus the gauge's true error. [PLACEHOLDER] limit 6.9 kPa (1 psi, about 2 x the gauge MPE) and 20 CR petty fine are the agent's picks, not researched; tune in playtest.

flares._note: Solar flare nights, when Kestrel trades. A fixed schedule by the clock; every number is [PLACEHOLDER]. A flare has to end before the next 06:00.

oirm._note: Orbital Institute of Reference Measures (working name). A standard rides Vance's drop pod after an audit and returns on the next one with a certificate. On any other day it can go by courier for the fee plus courier_surcharge_credits and returns courier_return_days later (Ryan, 2026-11-22). Fee, surcharge and days are placeholders (docs/design/equipment_skills_robots.md section 1.7).

audit_schedule._note: Inspector Vance + AUD-1T land every 5th morning (docs/canon.md). Departure uses a wall-clock hour. Hours before the game day's start belong to the following calendar morning of the same game day.

calibration_interval._note: Interval adjustment (Ryan, 2026-11-21): as-found out of tolerance shortens the interval; an on-time calibration that passes lengthens it; a late pass keeps it. Day counts are placeholders.

calibration_uncertainty._note: operator_fraction_of_mpe [PLACEHOLDER]: u_op of an unskilled operator, as a fraction of the unit's MPE; the Uncertainty skill shrinks it. U = k × RSS of u_spec, u_cert, u_res, u_op, u_robot. TUR = MPE / U. Acceptance limit A = √(MPE² − U²). Below tur_floor the bench refuses; tur_clean is the 4:1 mark (Ryan, 2026-11-22, Q5, Q7, Q13).
